chunks: Abi (may Allah have mercy on him) from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Marwak ibn 'Ubayd from a man from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

One who applies antimony containing alcohol in his eyes once, the Almighty Allah will rub a rod of fire in his eyes. He said: Indeed, the people of wine-drinking in this world from the wine-drinkers will die thirsty, will be assembled thirsty, and will enter the Hellfire thirsty.

key_terms.مُسِرٍ: wine or alcohol (from the root s-k-r, intoxication)
key_terms.مِیلٍ: a rod or stick (used metaphorically for a measure or instrument)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of applying antimony mixed with wine according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing a symbolic correspondence between the physical application of antimony mixed with wine and the spiritual state of the consumer. It highlights the unique eschatological punishment of 'thirst' (al-'Atash) for wine drinkers, signifying their insatiable desire for the drink even in the Hereafter, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegetical tradition regarding the sensory punishments of Hell.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 5. Abi (rah) from Muhammad b. Yahya from Muhammad b. Ahmad from Ya’qub b. Yazid from Marwak b. ’Ubayd from a man from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) that he said: “

One who applies antimony containing alcohol in his eyes once, the Almighty Allah will rub a rod of fire in his eyes. People who drink wine in this world will die thirsty, will be assembled on the Day of Judgment thirsty and will be thrown into Hell thirsty.”
